notes: All seven authors-retained candidates are included: Gaia DR2 4056475218139133568 (ID 10), Gaia DR2 4060422022558245248 (ID 15), Gaia DR2 4060841348825794432 (ID 17), Gaia DR2 4060875566737607936 (ID 19), Gaia DR2 4061174432075039488 (ID 20), Gaia DR2 4061839842728015360 (ID 22), and Gaia DR2 4062483636849326080 (ID 23). Their candidacy is based on VVV proper motions; the authors note that Gaia PMs do not concur but treat the Gaia astrometric solutions as unreliable because of significant excess noise, and they still propose all seven as HVS candidates (T:p5-b1, T:p6-b1, T:p8-b6). Radial velocities are required to confirm whether the stars are unbound (T:p7-b3). The Introduction sentence reporting two candidate hypervelocity RC stars (T:p2-b2) conflicts with the abstract and conclusion reporting seven candidates (T:p1-b12, T:p8-b6) and with Tables 1-3 (I:p5-b0, I:p6-b0, I:p8-b0; T:p5-b0, T:p6-b0, T:p8-b0); I treat the repeated seven-candidate result as authoritative and omit the contradictory two-candidate statement. The local ID numbers are secondary identifiers; their correspondence to the Gaia DR2 Source IDs is supported by Tables 1-3 (I:p5-b0, I:p6-b0, I:p8-b0; T:p5-b0, T:p6-b0, T:p8-b0).

HVS 10: For ID 10 / Gaia DR2 4056475218139133568, Table 3 (T:p8-b0) reports only a total proper-motion magnitude, 208.743 ± 28 mas/yr, rather than equatorial proper-motion components; no individual proper-motion components or radial velocity are reported. Therefore those quantities are not extracted. The Table 2 values (T:p6-b0) are the separate d_Ks and d_G_DR1 distance estimates.

HVS 15: At T:p8-b0, Table 3 reports only a total VVV proper-motion magnitude for ID 15 (269.609 ±23 mas/yr), not equatorial proper-motion components. At T:p3-b6 the paper describes excluding sources with well-defined parallaxes but gives no individual parallax value for ID 15. At T:p7-b3 and T:p8-b4 it states radial velocities are absent. Therefore proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactic rest-frame speed, and bound probabilities are not extracted.

HVS 17: The target HVS 17 (ID 17, Gaia DR2 4060841348825794432) has tabulated equatorial coordinates and two photometric distances. Table 3 (T:p8-b0) reports a single proper-motion magnitude, 171.367 ± 27 mas/yr, not separate equatorial proper-motion components, so it is not extracted as proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec. Table 3 also reports tangential velocity V_T = 5903.893 km/s, which is not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not extracted as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The paper states that radial velocities are absent (T:p7-b3), and no individual parallax, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for the target.

HVS 19: Target: HVS candidate ID 19 (Gaia DR2 4060875566737607936), one of the seven VVV proper-motion-selected candidates (T:p5-b1, T:p8-b6). Table 3 gives only the total proper-motion modulus (PM = 185.743 ± 26 mas/yr from VVV), not separate equatorial components, so no proper_motion_ra/proper_motion_dec values are recorded; likewise no individual RA/Dec proper motions are tabulated elsewhere. No radial velocities were measured (T:p7-b3, T:p8-b4). The paper reports a tangential velocity V_T = 6442.689 km/s (Table 3) derived from VVV PMs, but this is not a Galactic-rest-frame total speed, and no galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star, so these quantities are omitted. Two distances are reported (d_Ks and d_G_DR1); both are recorded.

ID 20: Table 3 at T:p8-b0 reports for ID 20 a single total proper-motion value, PM = 493.208 ±24 mas yr^-1, and no separate equatorial proper-motion components, so no proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec values were assigned. Its V_T = 17918.229 km s^-1 is explicitly a tangential velocity, not a total Galactic rest-frame speed, so it was not assigned to galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No radial velocity, parallax, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

HVS 22: Table 3 (T:p8-b0) reports a single VVV proper-motion magnitude for this star, 156.447 ± 30 mas yr^-1, rather than separate equatorial proper-motion components, so no proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec value is entered. No radial velocity is reported for this candidate; the paper explicitly calls for radial-velocity follow-up (T:p7-b3). The distance listed in Table 3 is numerically identical to d_Ks in Table 2 and is recorded once with that condition.

HVS 23: For ID 23, the paper lists a total proper-motion magnitude of 123.374 ± 31 mas yr^-1 in Table 3 (T:p8-b0), not equatorial proper-motion components, so proper_motion_ra and proper_motion_dec are omitted. Radial velocities are not reported (T:p7-b3), so radial_velocity is omitted; no Galactic-rest-frame total speed or bound probabilities are given.
